clue.text: Able to control waste output – mad having tried an alternative (5,7)

indicators.note: an alternative version of the letters is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A frazzled report on a mad experiment to manage some waste-producing output.
explanation.walkthrough: Potty means both crazy and a child's toilet, so the first half of the answer hides behind 'mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from the nursery: a child is potty-trained once it has learned to use the potty rather than a nappy.

clue.text: Toffs eating parsnip skins – they’re generally quite hot! (7)

indicators.note: the toffs take the other letters inside them
a parsnip's skins are its outside letters

explanation.surface: Posh diners tucking into parsnip peel at a dinner that turns out spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: Toffs are the lords of the peerage. 'Generally' covers the mild sweet varieties, keeping the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppers such as chillies are mostly hot to eat.

clue.text: Urban dwellers have connections all around (7)

indicators.note: the ties go all the way around the other word

explanation.surface: City folk are well networked on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' reads as a link word joining definition to wordplay, but it is working wordplay: a verb meaning possess.
explanation.definitionFit: Townies are people who live in towns, as opposed to country folk.

clue.text: It measures how tricky ads are broadcast (9)

indicators.note: scattered, sown widely, so the letters are spread about

explanation.surface: A survey gauging how devious the adverts on air are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as TV and radio in the surface; its job is to scatter the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measuring rod, and so a standard for measuring anything.

clue.text: Lots providing service on tables outside (5)

indicators.note: only the outside letters of 'tables' are used

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Waiters serving plenty of food at tables out on a terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' wants to be waiting at table; it is one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is a large number of them, as are lots.

clue.text: Where Rolls Royce is found for example – by mistake (2,5)

definitions.text: Where Rolls Royce is found for example

blocks.clueFragment: Where Rolls Royce is found for example
blocks.note: Rolls Royce abbreviates to RR; ask which everyday word has those two letters sitting in it

explanation.surface: A car found parked somewhere it should not have been.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic take: Rolls Royce is RR, and those two letters sit inside the word ERROR, so RR is found 'in ERROR'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in error means doing it by mistake.

clue.text: Therefore acquiring a business degree is a restriction (7)

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it

explanation.surface: A grumble that needing an MBA shuts people out of jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A business degree' is one piece, not A plus a degree; it slots in after the first letter of the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, a restriction on trade.

clue.text: Had neat field ploughed up – it’s really serious (4,3,5)

indicators.note: turned over like soil, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: A farmer's tidy field has been churned up, and it is a grave matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of HAD NEAT FIELD is used; the farming picture keeps 'ploughed up' looking literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A life-and-death matter is one of the utmost seriousness.

clue.text: Might follower of what’s fashionable get elected? (2,5)

blocks.note: power = might, and it follows IN

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a trend-chaser could win an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like the verb 'may'; it is the noun, strength. The question mark flags that elected is an example of being in power.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: winning an election is one way a party comes to hold office.

clue.text: Cheap hotel set in fine meadow land (7)

blocks.note: to land a fish is to bag it

explanation.surface: An advert for a budget hotel in fine meadowland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meadow land' reads as one idea; split it, and 'land' becomes the verb to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleabag is a seedy, cheap hotel, the sort you might catch fleas in.

clue.text: Grand antique banner is the best example of its kind (4,8)

definitions.text: the best example of its kind

blocks.note: a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: Praise for a magnificent old flag as the finest of its type.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand is British slang for a thousand pounds; a standard in the banner sense is a regimental flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The gold standard is the benchmark others are measured against.

clue.text: Opposition forces catholic out? (7)

blocks.note: the reading the setter meant: the people and armies ranged against you
the surface picture of a faction driving Catholics away, a religious red herring

explanation.surface: A question about whether a rival faction drove the Catholics away.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposing forces in any contest are the enemies; the tail reads as a religious expulsion to disguise that plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the forces ranged against you in any contest are your foes.

clue.text: Central resorts said to be sisterly (7)

indicators.note: only the central letters of 'resorts' are used

explanation.surface: A report that city-centre holiday spots are rated as friendly as sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' is not a sound-alike signal here; it gives ORAL, as in an oral agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sororal, from Latin soror, means of or like a sister.

clue.text: Features of executioner’s equipment lacking nothing (5)

indicators.note: the equipment goes without one letter

blocks.note: O = zero, nothing; one O is removed

explanation.surface: A grim inventory of a hangman's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' is the face sense: a nose is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Features' in the sense of parts of the face, of which the nose is the most prominent.

clue.text: Being this arrogant about victory might be unfeeling (9)

indicators.note: the answer goes about V to make the word for unfeeling

explanation.surface: A warning that gloating over a win can look heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer placed about V becomes IMPERVIOUS, so the answer is IMPERVIOUS with the V taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperious means arrogantly domineering.

clue.text: It gives permission to report as crowd get through (5,4)

blocks.note: pass = get through, as an exam

explanation.surface: A reporter squeezing through a throng to get to the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd' is the noun press, a throng, not the journalists the answer is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A press pass lets a journalist into events to report on them.

clue.text: I know nothing about academic work on compiler (4,3,2)

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher
the compiler (setter) refers to themself as ME

explanation.surface: A disclaimer about a scholar's paper on some compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: The compiler is the setter of the puzzle, so it gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'don't ask me' is admitting you know nothing about it.

clue.text: Attitude adopted by aristocrat over independent African capital (7)

indicators.note: the attitude is taken into the aristocrat
in a down clue, placed above the next piece

explanation.surface: A snooty noble looking down on an independent African city.
explanation.walkthrough: Nob is British slang for a posh person, and an air is a manner someone adopts.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Nairobi is Kenya's capital city.

clue.text: Unwilling to join in adult party (7)

blocks.note: party as an informal get-together, a noun

explanation.surface: Someone hanging back from a grown-ups' party.
explanation.walkthrough: A for adult is the old film-certificate letter; the party is a get-together, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding social contact.

clue.text: Character initially seen in Greece – maybe Athens? (5)

indicators.note: take the initial letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of Seen In Greece Maybe Athens

explanation.surface: A figure spotted in Greece, perhaps in its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek setting is apt: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A character here is a letter, and sigma is the Greek S.

clue.text: Some Czechs met a native composer (7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the words that follow

blocks.note: hidden in czechS MET A NAtive

explanation.surface: Some Czech people meeting a local musician.
explanation.walkthrough: The hint is apt: Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Smetana wrote Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Donated place to house outrageous type of dance (7)

indicators.note: one piece is placed so as to hold the other inside

explanation.surface: Someone giving a venue for a wild dance.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is 'over the top', British slang for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the gavotte is an old French court dance in quick duple time.

clue.text: Operatic piece about drug free region in America (7)

definitions.note: elliptical: the definition leans on 'region' from the wordplay, reading as a region in America

indicators.note: the aria goes around the other piece
the region is freed of the drug

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: An opera song about a drug-free area in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Region' does double duty: it gives ZONE and is also part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Arizona is one of the southwestern states of the USA.

clue.text: Offence caused by cleric who has lost the head (5)

indicators.note: a word that has lost its head has lost its first letter, the top of the word

blocks.note: P is removed from the front

explanation.surface: A crime blamed on a vicar who lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost the head' reads as losing one's temper; here it strips the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Suspended woman was deprived of information (7)

indicators.note: the word for 'was' loses a letter

explanation.surface: A woman was hanged, or was kept in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspended' pulls towards hanging; it means put on hold. I for information is the tourist-sign symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a plan put on the shelf is set aside, suspended rather than cancelled.

clue.text: Clothing that is worn by criminals? (7)

indicators.note: the criminals wrap around, wear, the other piece

explanation.surface: Asking whether some garment is the uniform of lawbreakers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoodies do have a reputation as criminal wear, which the question mark nods to.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoodies are hooded sweatshirts, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Device supplied by poster fitter (7)

blocks.note: an ad is a poster, an advert

explanation.surface: A gadget provided by the person who puts up posters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitter' looks like a tradesman; it is the comparative adjective, more fit.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter is a device connecting incompatible parts.

clue.text: Scandal about fees charged in London market (12)

indicators.note: a -gate scandal is about something named before it

explanation.surface: Outrage over fees charged at a London market.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix -gate, from Watergate, is added to a word to name a scandal about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate is London's famous fish market.
